label: The short v4.0.1.0 entry is 196 lines: 20 frontmatter lines, 176 body lines, 11 H2 sections, 22 H4 items and no table in the body.
The cut is 42 percent and lands in one commit: bc28fcbbba is 338 lines, b6147d785b is 194, a8cc47730b is 196, HEAD is 196; no later commit restores a cut section.
Every H2 domain survives the cut in the same order: both versions carry the same 11 H2 headings, so the cut is taken at H4 level and no domain is deleted.

The H4 count falls from 38 to 22 (42 percent), matching the line cut: Skill Routing 6 to 3, Frontend 4 to 3, Doctor 6 to 5, Spec Kit 4 to 2, Playbooks 3 to 1, Retired 3 to 3, Runtimes 7 to 2, Clearer Skill Docs 5 to 3.
The exemplar cannot supply the length rule: v4.0.0.0 is 535 lines with 12 H2 and 40 H4 sections, 2.7 times the short entry, and the template calls it one in six hundred lines.

A cut H4 leaves the entry through one of three doors chosen by the reader need to act: folded into a neighbouring H4 as a closing sentence, folded into one bullet list under one H4, or dropped entirely.

The folded-fixes container is one H4 named Smaller Fixes with four bold-lead bullets that absorb five long-version H4 items; a sixth, The Git Advisory Keeps the Directory, is dropped even from the folded list.
Every surviving H4 in the short entry is exactly one paragraph and the body carries exactly one bullet list; the long version carries bullet lists inside five body H4 items.

Part of the diff is packet renumbering, not format: the long spec line names specs/sk-doc/072, specs/agents/021 and 042, the short one names specs/sk-doc/051-hub-routing-quality/002, specs/agents-md/016 and no 042, while 043 and commands/005 are unchanged.

The spec line compresses to nine folders with no level or phase annotation and one trailing clause, "with smaller packets for the fixes", against a long single paragraph referencing more than twenty packets each with Level or phase annotations.
Upgrade Notes is 16 plain bold-condition bullets ordered to match the body section order, and it does not use the Adopt, Repoint and Drop lead-in triad.
The component cross-reference is a single sentence in the last body section naming every component and mode that has its own changelog entry.

The format-selection guide mandates the long branch for this release: 10 or more changes takes Expanded, and any breaking change takes Expanded regardless of count, which excludes the short entry outright.
The length table has a Compact file-total ceiling of 40 prose lines and no Expanded file-total row, so a many-change release has no file-level ceiling at all.

The template contradicts itself on two counts that the short entry resolves against the template: the exemplar-wins clause plus the sit-beside-the-exemplar requirement point at 535 lines, and the (Level N) spec-line shape block contradicts the Drop list ban on phase numbers.
A generated release entry preserves every H2 domain and takes the entire cut at H4 level.
A release with 10 or more changes or any breaking change has a file-level length target, not only an unbounded Expanded branch.
A spec-folder line carries folder paths only: no Level annotation and no phase number.

The current template already carries compact and expanded shapes, a keep and drop list and a cut test, so the residual long-format pressure is concentrated in the format-selection guide, the missing expanded file ceiling, the exemplar-wins clause and the spec-line shape block.
